components.heading: Linux Lab 01: A Correct epoll Echo Loop

payload.title: A Correct epoll Echo Loop
payload.summary: Build a one-connection Linux event loop that preserves application state while readiness notifications, partial I/O, peer shutdown, signals, and a deadline compete.

prerequisites: Complete the stream-socket and TCP reliability lessons first
Understand that TCP streams do not preserve message boundaries
Understand that send may consume fewer bytes than requested
Build only on Linux with TCPIP_BUILD_LINUX_LABS enabled
outcomes: Explain why edge-triggered code drains an operation to EAGAIN
Use a bounded work quantum for level-triggered readiness
Keep unread input and unsent output as separate state

events.label: Create constrained socketpair
events.detail: test_large_echo creates a local stream socketpair and requests 2048-byte send and receive buffers on both endpoints.

events.label: Prepare 256 KiB payload
events.detail: The deterministic TEST_PAYLOAD_SIZE body is much larger than the socket buffers and the echo loop's fixed 16 KiB buffer.

events.label: Start mismatched quanta
events.detail: peer_exchange makes its endpoint nonblocking, sends at most 701 bytes, and receives at most 389 bytes per ready pass.

events.label: Preserve flags and arm deadline
events.detail: tcpip_linux_l01_echo saves the caller's flags, enables O_NONBLOCK if needed, and computes one 5000 ms CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadline.

events.label: Register read interest
events.detail: The loop creates its own epoll descriptor and registers EPOLLIN plus EPOLLRDHUP, with EPOLLET only for edge-triggered mode.

events.label: Report readiness
events.detail: epoll_wait returns a readiness event; a signal retries with the remaining time instead of restarting the deadline.

events.label: Read partial stream bytes
events.detail: recv appends bytes without overwriting pending output; edge mode drains toward EAGAIN while level mode spends one bounded read quantum.

events.label: Enable write interest
events.detail: Pending bytes add EPOLLOUT to the interest set while unread capacity and unsent output remain separate state.

events.label: Write partial echo bytes
events.detail: send with MSG_NOSIGNAL advances only by the returned count; backpressure can leave bytes pending for another readiness event.

events.label: Repeat readiness cycles
events.detail: EAGAIN completes a nonblocking drain, and the read/write cycle repeats until all 262144 bytes cross in both directions.

events.label: Verify and clean up
events.detail: The test checks byte-for-byte equality, counters, edge drains, exact flag restoration, and closure of the temporary epoll descriptor.

rows: Shows how often epoll_wait delivered work
Includes calls that finish a nonblocking drain with EAGAIN
Includes calls that meet backpressure with EAGAIN
Reaches expected_bytes on a successful large echo
Reaches expected_bytes only after pending output drains
Makes completed nonblocking read drains observable
Makes completed nonblocking write drains observable
Exposes work performed while draining edge-triggered readiness

payload.exercise: Implement exercise.c without changing lab.h or the tests. Validate arguments, initialize stats before early returns, use fixed local storage, preserve descriptor flags, and treat EINTR as a retry without resetting the absolute deadline.
payload.reference: Compare against the reference implementation through the linux-reference preset after the starter compiles.
checks: Large level-triggered and edge-triggered echoes preserve content and byte counts
Descriptor flags are restored and the temporary epoll descriptor does not leak
Edge-triggered paths record completed nonblocking drains
Zero-length work, invalid descriptors, invalid triggers, null stats, negative timeouts, EOF, truncation, and bounded timeout are deterministic

allowed: A one-connection teaching loop using a caller-owned connected descriptor
Local Unix socketpair endpoints in tests
MSG_NOSIGNAL to suppress SIGPIPE for individual sends
excluded: Changing process signal disposition or closing the caller's socket
An accept loop, connection table, cancellation API, TLS, or application framing protocol
Promises to echo bytes beyond the requested boundary or diagnose application messages
